title: 2026-11-05_Linux_AirDropBot_Botnet_Investigation_638
description: Investigate a compromised host running the Linux/AirDropBot botnet malware.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Linux/AirDropBot is a multiplatform Linux malware that functions as a backdoor and botnet. It has infection capabilities targeting vulnerabilities in routers CGI or telnet. The malware can perform TCP, UDP, and custom pattern DDoS attacks. It connects to a C2 server to receive commands and can spread via exploiting vulnerabilities.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the scenario.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the following credentials to access the system:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano
Enter 'start' to begin the scenario.

levels.title: Identify the C2 Beacon Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server.
levels.solution:
1. Log in to the bot1 host using the provided credentials.
2. List all services to identify any unusual or suspicious services.
   - Command: `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`
3. Look for services with unusual names or descriptions that might indicate malicious activity.
4. Identify the service responsible for sending beacon to the C2 server.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl` command to list all services and look for any that seem out of place.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the service descriptions and paths to identify any suspicious services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for services that might be related to network communication or system health monitoring.

levels.title: Determine the Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Log in to the bot1 host using the provided credentials.
2. Inspect the service identified in the previous task to find the network port associated with the communication.
   - Command: `systemctl cat bot-beacon-cloudprocess.service`
3. Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service file to identify the script path.
4. Examine the script to find the network port used for communication.
   - Command: `cat /usr/local/lib/.botcache/beacon.sh`

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service file to identify the script path.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Examine the script to find the network port used for communication.

levels.title: Identify the Scheduling Timer
levels.content: Investigators suspect how the C2 beacon service automatically resumes after the system starts and continues to execute periodically. Determine which system component is responsible for scheduling this activity.
levels.solution:
1. Log in to the bot1 host using the provided credentials.
2. List all timers to identify any unusual or suspicious timers.
   - Command: `systemctl list-timers --all`
3. Look for timers with unusual names or descriptions that might indicate malicious activity.
4. Identify the timer responsible for scheduling the C2 beacon service.
